_why: The explicit provider allowlist for the resource layer. A host that is not here is external-only: no provider is inferred from a URL, and no iframe is built from a URL the policy has not named. `mechanism` is the presentation the provider is allowed to use, not a promise that its headers still permit it; the build-time embed report and the resolver both have to agree. `sandbox` and `allow` are copied verbatim into the frame for that provider, so a permissive token is a reviewed decision rather than a default. `license.reuse` is the permission verdict; `license.conditions` names the obligations a Reader Mode snapshot must carry (notice, attribution, share-alike, non-commercial, ...). An `allowed` verdict is not a claim that those obligations are already met.

providers.sandbox: allow-scripts allow-same-origin allow-forms allow-popups allow-popups-to-escape-sandbox allow-downloads
providers.evidence: No X-Frame-Options or frame-ancestors denial. It sends no CORP, so the frame is loaded credentialless: the app keeps COEP require-corp for SharedArrayBuffer, and the embedded course gets no credentials or shared storage. The root LICENSE.txt is MIT and covers the course chapters; text/code snapshots are clear with its notice, while images and linked videos need a per-asset check.

No X-Frame-Options or frame-ancestors denial. It sends no CORP, so the frame is loaded credentialless; PSF-2.0 covers the documentation and permits reproduction with its licence and copyright notice plus a change summary. Examples and recipes are also 0BSD; no snapshot is stored.
